# DeliveryIQ — Stage 4 Modelling Report

**Generated by:** `src/modelling.py` on 2026-10-31 (runtime 260.5 s) · **Status:** awaiting owner review  
**Every number is read from `reports/modelling_metrics.json`.** The test set was used once, after all decisions were made on training data.

## 1. Headline results (held-out test set)

Test period **2022-03-30 → 2022-04-06** (8,470 orders). Models trained on **2022-02-11 → 2022-03-29** (37,123 orders).

| Task | Selected model | Test result | Baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| ETA regression (order placement) | Histogram gradient boosting | MAE **6.19 min** · RMSE 7.73 · R² **0.310** | median: MAE 7.47 · RMSE 9.31 · R² -0.000 |
| Late risk, > 30 min (project benchmark) | Histogram gradient boosting | ROC-AUC **0.791** · PR-AUC **0.608** · precision 0.467 · recall 0.813 · F1 0.593 (threshold 0.268) | prior: ROC-AUC 0.500 · PR-AUC 0.287 (= prevalence) |
| Delivery zones | K-Means, k = 22 | silhouette **0.948** | — |

The ETA model cuts test MAE by **17.1%** against the median baseline (1.28 min per order). It explains about 31% of the variance in delivery time, using only information available when the order is placed.

## 2. Protocol

- **Chronological split** on whole order dates: train ≤ 2022-03-29, test ≥ 2022-03-30 (37,123 / 8,470 rows).
- **Tuning and selection on the training split only,** with 3 forward-chaining CV folds. Each fold validates on later dates than it trains on:
  - Fold 1: train 9,394 rows → validate 9,692 rows (2022-03-03 → 2022-03-11)
  - Fold 2: train 19,086 rows → validate 9,540 rows (2022-03-12 → 2022-03-20)
  - Fold 3: train 28,626 rows → validate 8,497 rows (2022-03-21 → 2022-03-29)
- **Preprocessing** (median / most-frequent imputation, scaling, one-hot) sits inside each sklearn pipeline, so it is fitted on training rows only, per fold and for the final model. No missing-indicator columns.
- **Leakage guard:** inputs only via `get_model_inputs()`; the primary feature sets pass the strict guard. Comparison models need an explicit `allow_excluded=True` and are labelled as such.
- **Selection rules:** regression by lowest CV MAE; classification by highest CV PR-AUC; decision threshold by maximum F1 on out-of-fold training predictions; zones by maximum silhouette.

### `city_code` availability review [owner request]

The dataset has **no independent order-time city field**: the raw `City` column is a city *type*. On geo-valid rows the city is fully implied by the restaurant coordinates (100% recoverable by nearest centroid), and those are already features. On the 3,640 geo-invalid rows the rider-ID prefix is the only source, and that is rider-assignment information. **`city_code` is therefore excluded from the primary model** and added to the leakage guard's excluded list. The primary set is 14 features.

## 3. Feature-variant decisions (made on training CV only)

Rule (pre-registered): CV MAE tolerance 0.5%; drop order_month unless it improves CV MAE by more than the tolerance; exclude a training subset only if that improves CV MAE by more than the tolerance. Decided with hist_gbm (best CV family on primary set).

| Variant | Train rows | CV MAE | Test MAE (all) | Test MAE (time present) | Test MAE (time missing) | Test R² |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Order placement, 14 features (with `order_month`) | 37,123 | 6.288 | 6.187 | 6.164 | 6.774 | 0.311 |
| Order placement without `order_month` | 37,123 | 6.295 | 6.194 | 6.171 | 6.791 | 0.310 |
| Order placement; 1,731-row missing-time block removed from training | 35,709 | 6.318 | 6.203 | 6.156 | 7.420 | 0.309 |
| Order placement; missing-Festival rows removed from training | 36,944 | 6.278 | 6.176 | 6.156 | 6.712 | 0.314 |
| **Comparison only:** + rider age & rating, vehicle, batching, weather, traffic | 37,123 | 3.557 | 3.498 | 3.424 | 5.413 | 0.779 |
| **Comparison only:** as above without rider rating | 37,123 | 3.823 | 3.671 | 3.600 | 5.495 | 0.762 |

**Decisions:**
- `order_month`: **dropped**. CV MAE 6.288 with vs 6.295 without, so the month adds nothing measurable, and April is never seen in training.
- Missing-time block (1,731 rows): **kept in training**. Removing it worsens CV MAE (6.318) and sharply worsens test error on those orders (7.42 vs 6.77 min).
- Missing-Festival rows (228): **kept**. CV MAE 6.278 vs 6.288, a 0.16% change, which is below the 0.5% rule.
- **Final primary feature set (13):** `distance_km`, `restaurant_lat`, `restaurant_lon`, `order_hour`, `order_hour_sin`, `order_hour_cos`, `order_day_of_month`, `order_is_weekend`, `city_type`, `order_type`, `festival`, `order_time_band`, `order_day_of_week`.

## 5. Late-delivery classification (> 30 min, project benchmark — not an official SLA)

Test prevalence: 28.7%.

| Model | Params | CV ROC-AUC | CV PR-AUC | Threshold | Test precision | Test recall | Test F1 | Test ROC-AUC | Test PR-AUC | Brier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prior baseline (constant) | `{}` | 0.500 | 0.300 | 0.500 | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.500 | 0.287 | 0.205 |
| Logistic regression | `{'C': 10.0}` | 0.746 | 0.560 | 0.213 | 0.402 | 0.900 | 0.556 | 0.766 | 0.570 | 0.166 |
| Histogram gradient boosting ★ | `{'learning_rate': 0.05, 'max_leaf_nodes': 15, 'l2_regularization': 0.0}` | 0.779 | 0.595 | 0.268 | 0.467 | 0.813 | 0.593 | 0.791 | 0.608 | 0.159 |

★ selected by highest chronological-CV PR-AUC on the training split. The prior baseline predicts no late orders at 0.5, so its precision, recall and F1 are 0; this is why accuracy alone is never reported.

### Decision threshold

- **Default: 0.268**, the F1-maximising threshold on out-of-fold *training* predictions (out-of-fold precision 0.471, recall 0.807).
- **Why not 0.5:** 29% of test orders are late. A missed late order (no proactive customer message, no dispatch attention) usually costs more than a false alarm (an unnecessary heads-up). A threshold below 0.5 trades precision for recall.
- **Recall ≥ 80% alternative:** 0.273 → test precision 0.468, recall 0.809, F1 0.593. At this benchmark it nearly coincides with the F1 point.
- **Confusion matrix at the default threshold (test):**
  - 1,978 late orders caught; 454 missed.
  - 2,259 false alarms; 3,779 correctly cleared.
- **Orders with an order time** (what the demo sees): ROC-AUC 0.794, PR-AUC 0.611, F1 0.597.

Charts: `figures/16_classification_roc_pr.png`, `figures/17_classification_threshold.png`, `figures/18_confusion_matrix.png`.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| > 30 min | 28.7% | 0.268 | 0.467 | 0.813 | 0.593 | 0.791 | 0.608 | 2.1× |

## 6. Comparison: what dispatch-time information adds (NOT deployable at order placement)

Adding rider age and rating, vehicle, batching, weather and traffic cuts test MAE from 6.19 to **3.50 min** (R² 0.779). Late-risk ROC-AUC rises to 0.983. Without rider rating: MAE 3.67, ROC-AUC 0.952.
- These fields are excluded from the primary model by owner decision: they are unknown at order placement, or have unverified recording times or leakage risk.
- The gap is the value of a **two-stage ETA**: a placement-time estimate, refreshed once a rider is assigned. That is a Stage 5 recommendation candidate, not a claim about deployable accuracy.
- Part of the rating effect may be leakage (a rating could include this delivery's feedback), so the no-rating figures are the safer reference.

**Interpretation:**
- Every zone contains exactly one city code, so the zones are the **22 cities**. Delivery points are synthetic offsets around restaurants (Stage 1), so finer intra-city zones are not supported by the data.
- Late rates vary only from 28.7% to 34.3% across zones. **Location explains little of the delay**; the stronger drivers are in §4's importance table.
- **Zone volumes are uneven because invalid locations are concentrated by city.** Overall 8.0% of orders have no valid location, but VAD 50.2%, DEH 33.2%, BHP 30.8%. Those cities are under-represented in the zone counts, and their zone profiles rest on fewer orders.
- Rider segmentation: not performed — delivery_person_id is not a person identifier (Stage 1 audit).

## 8. Validation checks

| # | Check | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | train and test disjoint; every train date < every test date | ✅ pass | cut 2022-03-30 |
| 2 | CV folds use training rows only and validate on later dates | ✅ pass | 3 forward-chaining folds |
| 3 | primary feature sets pass the strict leakage guard; city_code absent | ✅ pass | 14 features |
| 4 | label-permutation sanity (10 shuffles): ridge on shuffled targets has mean test R² ≤ 0.01 and max < selected model R² | ✅ pass | mean R² -0.0032, max 0.0080 |
| 5 | selected ETA model beats the median baseline on test MAE | ✅ pass | 6.194 vs 7.474 |
| 6 | label-permutation sanity (20 shuffles): mean test ROC-AUC within 0.5 ± 0.03 and max < selected model ROC-AUC | ✅ pass | mean 0.4918 (sd 0.0668, max 0.6092) vs model 0.7911 |
| 7 | decision threshold chosen on out-of-fold TRAINING predictions only | ✅ pass |  |
| 8 | clustering uses geo-valid rows only (no missing coordinates) | ✅ pass |  |
| 9 | saved ETA model reloads and reproduces test predictions exactly | ✅ pass |  |
| 10 | ETA model refit is deterministic (seeded) | ✅ pass |  |
| 11 | saved late-risk model reloads and reproduces test probabilities exactly | ✅ pass |  |
| 12 | raw, cleaned and engineered datasets unchanged (SHA-256) | ✅ pass |  |

**12 / 12 passed.**

**Finding on the label-permutation check:** a first version shuffled the labels once and expected test ROC-AUC near 0.5. It failed (0.565). Repeating the shuffle showed why:
- Over 20 shuffles, AUC averages **0.492** (sd 0.067, range 0.354–0.609), with 45% above 0.5. That is symmetric around 0.5, so no leakage.
- A model fitted to noise has a random coefficient direction, and a random combination of *informative* features correlates, positively or negatively, with the true labels.
- The check now tests the distribution, and requires the real model to beat every shuffled run.

## 9. Limitations

- **Modest primary accuracy by design:** without dispatch-time fields, test R² is 0.310 and the late-risk F1 is 0.593. This is the honest order-placement level of accuracy for this dataset.
- **Short test window:** 8 days (2022-03-30 → 04-06) inside an 8-week dataset. No seasonality can be assessed, and all CV folds fall in March.
- **Synthetic data patterns** (Stage 1): 5-minute target blocks, diagonal delivery offsets, traffic set by hour. Metrics may not transfer to real operations.
- **Median imputation** treats the 3,640 geo-invalid and 1,731 missing-time orders as typical orders. Their errors are higher (see segments).
- **Models are trained on the training split only** and are not refitted on all data, so the saved models are exactly the ones evaluated. A production refit on all 45,593 rows would be a separate, documented step.
- **Hyper-parameters were tuned on the primary set** and reused for the variants and the final set. Variant comparisons are therefore not fully re-tuned.
- **Probabilities are not calibrated:** Brier scores are reported; calibration is not checked yet.
- **The comparison model's rating effect** may include leakage.
